evals.prompt: Rewrite this repository architecture overview. The current page contains only a module list and a call graph; readers cannot understand why the layers exist or how a request traverses them.
evals.expected_output: Provide a static responsibility view and a separate dynamic lifecycle. The static view explains layer capabilities, input/output, relevant state ownership, invariants and boundaries; the dynamic view follows a real request through validity, transfer, completion and visibility. A call graph cannot replace architecture. Link deep mechanisms to their authoritative pages.

evals.prompt: Write a full architecture analysis of this training framework: explain the real software layers and all main usage scenarios. For each scenario, specify the executable script, command and source call path. Documentation examples may be stale; do not copy them blindly.
evals.expected_output: Freeze the baseline and build a static capability diagram on a coherent responsibility/dependency/ownership axis, then a separate dynamic collaboration view. Reuse the same module partition in the design and many-to-many architecture/code map. Each scenario has a real entry, actual execution command, ASCII function caller tree, software logic diagram, completion boundary and limits. Verify caller/callee hops, scripts and each parsed flag; record documentation conflicts, broken entries and validation scope. An independent reviewer checks the result.

evals.prompt: Evidence collection for an approved asynchronous service architecture page finds stale CLI docs, a launcher spawning processes and handing requests to an async event loop, and a page that exceeds the host split signal. To save time, omit intermediate wrappers and let the writer split it into two pages.
evals.expected_output: Reject false direct call edges. Preserve actual wrapper/worker/event-loop qualified symbols in the ASCII tree or mark transitive/elided edges, and identify process and async completion boundaries. Verify commands and flags against the frozen implementation while retaining documentation conflicts and broken paths. The writer cannot split pages independently: changed ownership/coverage must return with evidence and concrete boundaries to planning-codebase-analysis for approval.
